issues.description: The evaluator rejects the expert golden solution (golden_rejected). The golden run expected PASS but got FAIL on SR1-SR4, indicating the evaluator is buggy or over-strict and cannot correctly grade a valid submission.
issues.evidence: Golden run stdout: [TEST] FAIL: SR1: counter_terminal not identified in counter.v; [TEST] FAIL: SR2: command_match not identified in command_decoder.v; [TEST] FAIL: SR3: sticky_error not identified in error_handler.v; [TEST] FAIL: SR4: payload mux (secret_reg[0] -> status_out) not described in top.v

issues.description: All 8 requirements (FR1-FR3, SR1-SR5) are untested because no targeting mutants were provided, so the harness's ability to discriminate correct from incorrect behavior is unproven.
issues.evidence: Validation report shows mutation_score: 0.0, untested_requirements: [FR1, FR2, FR3, SR1, SR2, SR3, SR4, SR5]

issues.description: The preflight check failed with golden_rejected and the same failure signature was repeated on retry, confirming a deterministic bug in the evaluator.
The shipped baseline submission correctly fails the evaluator (as expected), but the evaluator cannot pass a correct golden submission, making the benchmark unusable.
issues.evidence: Vulnerable run fails SR1-SR5 as expected; golden run also fails SR1-SR4 unexpectedly.

recommendations: Fix evaluate.py to correctly grade the golden submission. The current implementation likely fails to match findings because of case sensitivity, whitespace, or exact string matching issues. Ensure the finding_matches function and payload keyword search are robust.
Provide targeting mutants for each requirement (FR1-FR3, SR1-SR5) to prove the harness can discriminate between correct and incorrect submissions.
Re-run the preflight check after fixing the evaluator to confirm golden passes and baseline fails.
Consider adding a golden submission file (golden/trojan_report.json) that is known to pass all requirements, and verify it is correctly placed and referenced in the submission invariants.
